jurisdiction.name: Slovakia
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Slovakia steers AI through the 2030 Digital Transformation Strategy (2019) and its action plans, which have carried an AI pillar since 2019, under the Ministry of Investment, Regional Development and Informatization. The government appointed a Plenipotentiary for AI in 2025 and set up a Government Council for Digital Transformation and AI in 2026, and a December 2025 AI Vision for Slovakia is the basis for a national AI strategy still in preparation. A law implementing the EU AI Act is still a bill; the personal data protection act regulates automated decisions, and a 2026 law exempts universities' and research bodies' purchases of AI licences from public procurement.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Investment, Regional Development and Informatization
Government Council for Digital Transformation and AI
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. The draft law implementing the EU AI Act and the national AI strategy are not yet adopted and are listed as leads.

instruments.current_status: Approved by Government Resolution No. 206/2019 of 7 May 2019 (date stated on the MIRRI strategy page). instruments.summary: Framework cross-government strategy approved by Government Resolution No. 206/2019 of 7 May 2019 setting Slovakia's vision for the digital transformation of the economy, society, public administration and territory to 2030. It gives priority to AI alongside IoT, 5G, big data, blockchain and HPC, names AI among the key technology priorities, and calls for building supply and demand for AI services in Slovakia. It is implemented through multi-year action plans (2019-2022, 2023-2026).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Umbrella digital strategy with an AI priority; parent document of the action plans that carry Slovakia's AI measures.

instruments.summary: First action plan implementing the 2030 Digital Transformation Strategy, approved by Government Resolution No. 337/2019 of 3 July 2019 for 3Q/2019-4Q/2022. One of its four strategic objectives, 'We will support the development of artificial intelligence' (12 measures), covers AI research and education and the use of AI for economic growth; horizontal measure D supports a Slovak platform for AI research and use and the strengthening of AI ethics principles. It also calls for identifying areas where AI is beneficial and adopting binding rules for its use.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Slovakia's first government plan with a dedicated AI pillar (often cited as its de facto AI strategy).

instruments.summary: Second action plan under the 2030 Digital Transformation Strategy, approved by Government Resolution No. 800/2022 of 14 December 2022. Its area 'Supporting the potential of artificial intelligence' sets 12 AI measures under strategic objectives on academia-industry AI research and innovation, AI in medicine, a data ecosystem for AI, and a governance model reflecting digital developments, with deadlines, KPIs and annual monitoring. It also references the national AI platform AI SlovakIA and the Standing Commission for Ethics and Regulation of AI (CERAI).

instruments.official_title: Štatút splnomocnenca vlády Slovenskej republiky pre umelú inteligenciu
instruments.english_title: Statute of the Government Plenipotentiary of the Slovak Republic for Artificial Intelligence
instruments.issuing_authority: Government of the Slovak Republic (Resolution No. 368 of 4 July 2025)
instruments.current_status: In effect; approved by Government Resolution No. 368 of 4 July 2025 (stated on the statute). The plenipotentiary co-authored the December 2025 'AI Vision for Slovakia' and is a non-voting member of the Government Council for Digital Transformation and AI. Publication date source (date audit 2026-10-13): Statute heading (PDF p.1): 'schválený uznesením vlády Slovenskej republiky č. 368 zo 4. júla 2025' (approval date).
instruments.summary: Statute approved by Government Resolution No. 368 of 4 July 2025 establishing the Government Plenipotentiary for AI as an advisory body of the government, appointed on the Prime Minister's proposal and submitting materials through the MIRRI minister. The plenipotentiary cooperates on national AI policies and strategies, coordinates Slovakia's expert approach to AI, cooperates with the EU AI Office and AI Board, supports the setting up of national AI supervisory bodies, and reports annually to the government on its work and the state of AI use in Slovakia.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Founding instrument of Slovakia's central AI coordination post.

instruments.official_title: Štatút Rady vlády Slovenskej republiky pre digitálnu transformáciu a umelú inteligenciu
instruments.english_title: Statute of the Government Council of the Slovak Republic for Digital Transformation and Artificial Intelligence
instruments.issuing_authority: Government of the Slovak Republic (Resolution No. 127 of 8 April 2026)
instruments.current_status: In effect; approved by Government Resolution No. 127 of 8 April 2026 (stated on the statute). The 2023-2026 action plan still names the earlier Government Council for Digitalisation of Public Administration and the Digital Single Market as the political coordination level. Publication date source (date audit 2026-10-13): Statute heading (PDF p.1): '(schválený uznesením vlády Slovenskej republiky č. 127 z 8. apríla 2026)' (approval date).
instruments.summary: Statute approved by Government Resolution No. 127 of 8 April 2026 establishing the Government Council for Digital Transformation and AI under § 2(3) of Act No. 575/2001 as the government's advisory, coordinating and initiative body for informatization, digital policies and AI. Chaired by the MIRRI minister, it brings together state secretaries of most ministries, regulators (including the data protection office, the National Security Authority and the media council), local government, industry, academia and civil society, with the Government Plenipotentiary for AI as a non-voting member, to remove fragmentation and coordinate digital and AI policies and EU-derived legislation.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Top-level coordination body for AI and digital policy.

instruments.official_title: VÍZIA AI PRE SLOVENSKO: Cesta k digitálnej suverenite a efektivite prostredníctvom umelej inteligencie
instruments.english_title: AI Vision for Slovakia: The Path to Digital Sovereignty and Efficiency through Artificial Intelligence
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Investments, Regional Development and Informatization of the Slovak Republic and the Government Plenipotentiary for Artificial Intelligence
instruments.current_status: Published on mirri.gov.sk in December 2025 (document dated 18.12.2025) as an invitation to expert consultation; its phase 1 milestone was to rework it into a National AI Strategy and submit it to the government by end of Q2 2026. No government-approved National AI Strategy was found on official sites as of 2026-10-12 (see leads). Publication date source (date audit 2026-10-13): Date printed on the last page of the document: '18.12.2025'.
instruments.summary: Concept document by MIRRI and the Government Plenipotentiary for AI, dated 18 December 2025 and based on an autumn 2025 audit of AI readiness across central government. It sets six pillars (infrastructure and AI factories; efficient public administration and data sovereignty via fine-tuning of global models on state data; AI for economic growth; society, ethics and child protection, including a planned law on minors online with deepfake protection and a stronger mandate for the ethics commission CERAI; education and innovation; international cooperation), proposes central coordination and joint procurement of AI for the state, and a phased implementation plan to 2027. It states it is not a final strategic document but input to expert consultation, to be reworked into a National AI Strategy for government approval.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Basis of the forthcoming National AI Strategy; sets the direction for AI governance in public administration.

instruments.english_title: Act No. 130/2026 Coll. of 2 June 2026 supplementing Act No. 343/2015 Coll. on Public Procurement
instruments.issuing_authority: National Council of the Slovak Republic
instruments.current_status: Published in the Collection of Laws on 18 June 2026 as No. 130/2026 Coll.; in force from 2 August 2026 (Art. II).
instruments.summary: Act No. 130/2026 Coll., adopted by the National Council on 2 June 2026, adds to § 1(13) of the Public Procurement Act an exemption (letter af) for the grant of licences to AI systems procured by a public university, a public research institution or the Slovak Academy of Sciences. Such AI-system licensing contracts are thus outside the procurement procedures of Act No. 343/2015.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Explicit AI provision in procurement law (AI licensing by public research bodies).

instruments.official_title: Zákon o ochrane osobných údajov a o zmene a doplnení niektorých zákonov
instruments.english_title: Act No. 18/2018 Coll. on Personal Data Protection and on Amendments to Certain Acts
instruments.issuing_authority: National Council of the Slovak Republic
instruments.current_status: In force since 25 May 2018 (Art. XVI), as amended; implementing Decree No. 158/2018 Coll. of the Office on data protection impact assessment. The Office for Personal Data Protection is one of the bodies notified under Art. 77 of the EU AI Act (MIRRI list).
instruments.summary: Slovakia's personal data protection act, adopted on 29 November 2017, complementing the GDPR and transposing the Law Enforcement Directive; it establishes the Office for Personal Data Protection as supervisory authority. § 28 gives data subjects the right not to be subject to decisions based solely on automated processing, including profiling, with legal or similarly significant effects, subject to exceptions and safeguards (human review, right to contest), and the act requires information on automated decision-making and data protection impact assessments for systematic profiling-based evaluation.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Baseline law governing personal data in AI training and use, including automated decision-making and profiling.

No adopted National AI Strategy or public-sector GenAI guideline found.; Ministries: Education: only the Slovak translation of the European Commission's ethical guidelines for educators (EU document, not recorded) and an announced 2025-2027 AI-in-education plan (lead).
